summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a statutory Small Business Commissioner to represent small businesses nationally, assist with disputes and investigate market practices that may adversely affect them.

The Commissioner could investigate complaints about Commonwealth bodies, facilitate business dispute resolution within constitutional limits and require relevant information, documents and attendance for questioning.
The existing Federal Small Business Commissioner would become the first statutory office holder, serving full time under appointment arrangements allowing terms of up to five years.
changes: The office would publish guidance on commercial dealings with Commonwealth bodies and undertake small business research.
The Commissioner could share information with the competition and corporate regulators.
People could be required to answer relevant questions under oath, with financial penalties for failing to attend.
An annual operations report would be presented to Parliament through the minister.
summary.affected: Small businesses, Commonwealth departments and agencies, other businesses in commercial disputes, and people required to provide information are affected.
